payload.title: PR-controlled opt-in gate lets Aleph integrity checks be bypassed
payload.description: The new gate reads `aleph.enabled` from the checked-out repository and all downstream verification jobs run only when `needs.gate.outputs.enabled == 'true'`. On pull requests, that checkout is attacker-controlled. A PR that modifies Aleph-managed files can also set `.loa.config.yaml` to `aleph.enabled: false`, causing the integrity workflow to no-op instead of verifying the changed third-party bundle. This creates a CI policy bypass for exactly the code the workflow is meant to protect.
payload.recommendation: Do not let PR contents decide whether required security/integrity jobs run. For PRs, read the opt-in value from the protected base branch, make Aleph path changes force verification regardless of the config diff, or keep the job running and fail/skip only non-security work after validating changed paths against a trusted policy source.
